lora_strength_note: MEASURED 2026-08-04 by studio/_tools/cast_motion.py stage `strength`, which is the downward sweep studio/loras/character-viro.json asked for and called 'a judgement, not a sweep'. Two places at the ends of the value range x three weights, one seed per place, IPAdapter held at 0.6: studio/samples/cast_motion/_strength.png. At 0.85 the scene is visibly flattened, and re-read at FULL RESOLUTION the subway cell is worse than first recorded: all five platform posters collapse into the SAME flat teal panel carrying a large orange 7. The LoRA is stamping the character's own jersey number onto the set dressing. The ladder is monotonic - at 0.00 the posters are five different designs with football icons and orange text bars, at 0.50 they are simplified but still five different glyphs, at 0.85 they are five copies of him. The snowfield's tree line hazes out the same way. CORRECTED 2026-08-04 ON REVIEW: the white patch on his forehead is NOT a strength discriminator and the first draft of this note was wrong to cite it as one. It is absent from both 0.50 cells and present in both 0.85 cells, which is what that draft saw - but it is also plainly present in the subway_platform strength 0.00 CONTROL in this same sheet, and in c3, c4, c6 and the LoRA-off x1 control of between.png, all of which ran at 0.50 or 0.00. It is a pipeline-wide artefact that comes and goes at every weight including zero. Do not read it as evidence about LoRA strength. At 0.50 the two-tone hair, the ponytail, the gold ear stud and the number 7 are all present and the room survives. 0.50 also matches what NIKA and PIP measured independently. THE CONTROL CELL IS WORTH READING TOO: at strength 0.00 the sheet alone still draws two-tone hair and a ponytail, but it puts the figure off-centre against the frame edge in both places - the LoRA is what centres him.
motion_verdict: YES, WITH ONE CONDITION - USE HIM, AND CUT BEFORE THE ACTION FINISHES. MEASURED 2026-08-04 by studio/_tools/cast_motion.py: 12 clips, one character, six places the training set never held, six different subject-motion cards, LoRA at the 0.50 measured above, IPAdapter 0.6, one video seed (7701) throughout, plus a LoRA-dropped control at the same keyframe seed and the same motion, plus 8-second re-renders of four of them. Every strip and every face strip was read. || THE STRUCTURAL FACT FIRST, because it decides what any of this can mean: THE CHARACTER LoRA IS NOT IN THE VIDEO GRAPH. short.py:394 splices node 90 into the anime KEYFRAME workflow only; workflows/12_ltx23_i2v_audio.json takes an image and a string. So BETWEEN clips identity is the LoRA's job and WITHIN a clip it is entirely LTX's, and no number on this card can help a shot that smears. || WITHIN A CLIP: HE HOLDS, AND HE HOLDS FOR EIGHT SECONDS. c1_walk_in_long is the cleanest evidence - at f192, 8.04s, the number 7 is still a clean orange 7, the gold ear studs are on BOTH ears, the two-tone pale-blond-over-brown hair and the top-knot are intact and the amber eyes are unchanged from the keyframe. The head-crop drift figure over that clip is non-monotonic (0-43-52-14-43-54-23-55-20), which is hair strands breathing, not a face going. NOTHING IN THIS RUN DEGRADED WITH TIME. || WHAT ENDS A FACE IS THE ACTION COMPLETING, NOT THE CLOCK - and this is the number that should change how shots are cut. head_turn and turn_away both give the face up, and they do it at a fraction of the clip rather than at a wall-clock second. c5_turn_away 4s: full face to f48 (2.0s), profile f60, back of head from f72 - gone at ~60% through. c2_head_turn 4s: face to f60 (2.5s), gone by f72 (3.0s) - ~70% through, reproducing that card's own documented overshoot from the whole body. c2_head_turn at 8s: FULL FRONTAL to f120 (5.0s), three-quarter at f144 (6.0s), clean PROFILE at f168 (7.0s), back of head at f192 (8.0s). DEFINE YOUR TERMS HERE, because the budget below depends on it: a first draft of this line said the face was GONE by f168, and read at full crop resolution that is not true - at f168 the eye is open, the gold ear stud is legible on the lobe and the two-tone hair and collar are intact. It is a usable profile. So: the last frame you can cut on for a FRONTAL OR THREE-QUARTER face is f144, 75% through; a legible PROFILE survives one step further to f168, 87% through; the face is genuinely gone only at f192. c6_step_back is the fastest loss: he turns and walks away instead of stepping back, and the face is gone by f48 (2.0s, ~50%). SO DOUBLING THE CLIP ROUGHLY DOUBLES THE FACE TIME. Budget about 60% of whatever length you ask for on a turning card, and put the cut there. || BETWEEN CLIPS: FIVE OF SIX ARE ONE MAN. studio/samples/cast_motion/between.png puts the best face from each 4s cell beside the reference sheet. WHAT HOLDS: the pale-blond crown over darker brown waves, the amber-brown eyes, the gold ear stud and the teal jersey with orange trim, in c1 (stadium concourse), c2 (snowfield), c4 (library) and c6 (market street). WHAT MOVES: the blond-to-brown RATIO swings hard - c1/c2/c5/c6 read predominantly blond, c3/c4 predominantly brown; the ear stud is GOLD in c1, c2, c4 and c6 and BLACK in c5; and c3 (subway platform) is the odd one out, with a rounder, younger, browner-haired face that would not cut against c2. The number 7 is clean in five places and garbled to something like a Pi or a 71 at market_street - and that happens in the KEYFRAME, before any video runs. || THE CONTROL, READ AT FULL RESOLUTION RATHER THAN OFF THE STRIP. x1_walk_in_nolora: same keyframe seed, same motion string, same video seed, LoRA 0.00, sheet still at 0.6. It is a DIFFERENT man, but not a wildly different one - the reference sheet at 0.6 is doing real work on its own, which is what cast_proof already found. THE ONE MARKER THAT SEPARATES THEM CLEANLY IS THE GOLD EAR STUD: a distinct gold stud on BOTH ears in every LoRA cell, and absent from every frame of the control. After that: the LoRA gives a pale blond crown gathered into a top-knot over brown waves, a narrow soft face with heavy-lidded amber eyes, and ONE large clean 7 centred on the chest. The control gives a blond crown fading into plain brown with no top-knot, a longer plainer face with round brown eyes, an orange polo collar rather than the orange V-neck, and the number rendered SMALL and high, DUPLICATED into a shield crest beside it. (A first draft of this verdict said the control had no number at all; that was read off a thumbnail and it is wrong. It has one, badly.) So the LoRA is what makes him a specific person and what makes the jersey read as a jersey. AND IT IS NOT WHAT MAKES HIM STABLE: the control's own drift curve is flat from 0.5s to 4.0s and flat again from 4.0s to 8.0s. Within-clip stability is LTX's image conditioning and it is there with or without a trained character. || WHAT ACTUALLY GOES WRONG, none of it identity: the LoRA still flattens a place at 0.50 - the stadium concourse rendered as an empty bleached corridor with none of the card's kiosks, turnstiles or litter, and rooftop_night rendered in broad daylight. A held prop drifts where a face does not: the white cup in c4 turns BLACK between 7 and 8 seconds. And the face this LoRA actually draws is soft and narrow, not the 'square jaw, heavy brows' studio/loras/character-viro.json claims. || A CAVEAT ABOUT THE MOTION LIBRARY, found in passing and worth its own job: THE CARDS' MEASURED NUMBERS DID NOT TRANSFER TO THESE KEYFRAMES. walk_in, the library's best card at a measured mean of 3.191, came back at 0.380 here - below its own do-nothing band - because c1's keyframe already has him close and there is nowhere to walk. Meanwhile hand_to_face, measured as a small articulated gesture at 0.62, walked him the entire length of a subway platform at 0.708, and cup_lift measured at 0.809 came back at 2.080. THE KEYFRAME'S STAGING, NOT THE MOTION STRING, DECIDED HOW MUCH MOVED. The library was measured on one keyframe; it needs re-measuring on several before its bands can be quoted at a user. || EVIDENCE: studio/samples/cast_motion/strips/*.png (12), faces/*.png (12), between.png, _strength.png, results.json. READ THE STRIPS - the metric ranked c4_cup_lift's drift at 108, the worst in the set, because he raises a cup in front of his own face on cue. That is the action landing, not the character leaving.

setting_verdict: CORRECTED 2026-08-04, and it overturns a finding this project reported twice as measured. The rule was 'a character LoRA at 0.85 destroys the setting' - observed on NIKA (a sunlit field became a grey void) and confirmed on TERRA (a snow forest collapsed to flat beige). BOTH OBSERVATIONS WERE REAL AND THE EXPLANATION WAS WRONG. It was never a property of LoRA strength. It was the UNCAPTIONED TAUPE BACKDROP of the turnaround being absorbed into the trigger: at high strength the LoRA reproduced its own training background over whatever place was asked for. Evidence at studio/samples/cast/terra_costume_fix/setting_grid.jpg - the v1 uncaptioned LoRA at 0.85 gives a featureless taupe void for snow_road and reduces a meadow to an arch-shaped window; the v3 LoRA, captioned and trained across two costumes, holds a real forest with depth and a real meadow at THE SAME 0.85 and the same seed. CONSEQUENCE: 0.85 is not inherently unsafe, and 0.5 was a workaround for a dataset defect rather than a law. The default stays 0.5 because that is what the rest of this character's evidence was measured at and nothing has yet shown 0.85 to be BETTER - only that it is no longer destructive. Any future character trained from an uncaptioned single-backdrop turnaround will reproduce the same defect, so caption the backdrop.
